mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced borrowing costs stimulate corporate investment and equity valuations through lower discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.5% annualized signals persistent inflation that triggers anticipated Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and high housing starts (HOUST > 1200.0) signal an overheating economy that triggers Fed policy tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and HOUST > 1200.0, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, high industrial production (INDPRO > 115.0) indicates peak economic activity and imminent policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO exceeds 115.0, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in late-cycle periods is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as robust residential construction signals strong consumer demand and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1200.0, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS decline > 0.25pp in 1 month) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals accommodative policy with strong labor conditions, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decline > 0.25pp in 1 month AND UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines by >0.25pp and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime, rising industrial production (INDPRO > 110.0) indicates economic recovery and improving corporate fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of early-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO exceeds 110.0, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in early-cycle periods is below 0.03.
